p.title: Riya's car count

ask.question: How many red cars did Riya see?

p.challenge: Read the tally: count the bundles in 5s (5, 10 ...), then add the single lines. How many red cars?
Deba made 12 marks when the cows went out. In the evening 9 cows come back: strike off 9 marks. How many cows are still out?

p.title: Letters in our names
p.challenge: Count the letters: RIYA, RAVI, NEHA, ARJUN, JOSEPH, HARPREET. Make a tally of how many names have each length.

p.title: Letters in each name
p.challenge: The captain must have the LONGEST name. Look at the letter counts and tap the longest name. (Which two names tie for shortest?)

p.title: First letters of names
p.challenge: Names: ARJUN, ANIL, BALA, ASHA, BHAVNA, CHETAN. Count how many start with A, with B and with C.
Build forty-seven. The tens word comes first (forty), then the ones word (seven).
Riddle: I am between 10 and 20. My name has 7 letters. I am odd. Drag the frog to me!

p.title: Eats food or not?
p.challenge: Sort a cow, a chair, a parrot, a ball and a fish by the rule "eats food / does not eat food". How many in each group?

p.title: Hairstyles in our class
p.challenge: Plait 8, Ponytail 5, Short hair 12, Bun 3. Which hairstyle is the LEAST common? Tap it.
Kabir has 12 marbles and Meena has 8. Count on from 8 to 12. How many more marbles does Kabir have?
A toy rocket's pointed top is a cone. Spin it: find its tip (Corners), its round flat face and its curved surface (Faces).
Raju wants to draw a tiger face on a shoe box (a cuboid). Tap Faces and Unfold net: how many flat faces can he choose from?

p.title: Parts of the toy rocket
p.challenge: A rocket model uses 1 cone, 2 cylinders and 4 cubes. Read the table. How many parts in all?

p.title: Build the model
p.challenge: Put the building steps in order. Then say: which shape is between the cuboid and the cone?
panels: First, put the cuboid at the bottom.
Then put the cube on top of the cuboid.
Then put the cone on top of the cube.
Now the cube is between the cuboid and the cone.

p.title: Straight or curved?
p.challenge: Pick a cube, cuboid, sphere, cylinder or cone. Answer the questions to name it.

nodes.info: Look at its faces and edges.
A curved surface bends. A flat face does not.
Check the bottom of the shape.

nodes.text: Cylinder or cone: flat faces and a curved surface
nodes.info: A candle is a cylinder. A birthday cap is a cone.
A brick or a matchbox. Not every cuboid is a cube.

p.title: Shapes in our classroom
p.challenge: Our list: 6 cuboids, 3 cylinders, 1 sphere, 2 cones. Which shape is the least common? Tap it.
A dice is a cube. Tap Faces, Edges and Corners. Check: 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners. Unfold the net to count the faces!
Turn the cylinder. It has 1 pair of opposite faces: its two round faces. Lay it down in your mind: is it still a cylinder?

p.title: Can it roll?
p.challenge: Test a sphere, a cube, a cuboid, a cylinder and a cone. Shapes with a curved surface can roll. Show how many roll and how many do not.

p.title: Copy the cube model
p.challenge: A model has 4 cubes in a row and 2 cubes on top. Put the building steps in order. Which cubes must go first?
panels: Put 4 cubes in a row on the table.
Put 2 cubes on top of the row.

p.challenge: Join 6 dice to make a cuboid: build 2 rows of 3 dice.
This is 15. Change it to 105 using the same digits 1 and 5. Where does the zero go, and what does it do?
A box holds 25 matchsticks. Hop in 25s. How many boxes of 25 make 100?
Which number comes just after 159? Drag the frog to it.
Show 1 big bundle of 100, 4 bundles of 10 and 7 loose sticks. Which number do you get?
What goes with 45 to make 100? Jump from 45 to 100 and add up your jumps.
Snakes and ladders: you are on 34 and want to land on 40. What should you roll? Hop to find out.
Build 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 3 ones. Why do we need the 0?
Compare 189 and 198. Hundreds are the same, so look at the tens. Drag the frog from 189 to 198: which is bigger?
Clap = 100, snap = 10, pat = 1. Clap, snap, snap, snap, pat, pat. Build that number!
Continue the jumps of 20: 120, 140, 160 ... Keep hopping to 200.
Nani Maa's trick: she has 20 seeds. You can see 13. How many are hidden (?)? Keep the scale level!
Add 7 + 5 like a tens frame: first hop 3 to fill up to 10, then hop 2 more.
Nani Maa picked 26 mangoes, then 18 more. Add 18 to 26. When the ones make 10, they become a new ten!
Nani Maa had 52 mangoes. Monkeys took 17. Take away 17. Not enough ones? Break a ten into 10 ones!
Fact family of 5, 8 and 13: solve 5 + ? = 13. Then say the other 3 facts!
52 stamps, 37 are Indian. 37 + ___ = 52. Jump from 37 to 40, then to 52. Add up the jumps.
Start at 53. Jump back by 10 three times. Only the tens beads change. Where do you land?
On the 1-100 grid, start at 45. Go down 3 rows (+3 tens), then right 4 (+4 ones). Where are you?
Magic square row: 2, 7, ___ must add to 15. 2 + 7 is 9. Find the missing number.
Add 85 + 67. Estimate first: about 90 + 70 = 160. Now add 6 tens and 7 ones to 85.
Box diagram: whole = 64 vadas, part 1 = 28. Jump from 28 to 64 to find part 2.
Open number line: start at 67 and jump 25 (two jumps of 10 and one of 5). Where do you land?
Find 58 + 9 the smart way: hop +10, then −1.

p.title: Shapes of things
p.challenge: Name the shapes: a ₹5 coin, a roti, a carrom board, a door, the front of a samosa. Show how many of each shape.
A toothpaste box is a cuboid. Press Unfold net to flatten it. Count the faces: what shape is each one?
Make a rectangle with 2 long sides of 5 units and 2 short sides of 3 units, like sticks. Opposite sides match!
p.winText: A rectangle: 2 long sides of 5 and 2 short sides of 3, with 4 square corners.

p.challenge: Change this rectangle into a SQUARE with every side 3 long. A square is a rectangle with all sides equal!
p.winText: A 3 by 3 square: 4 equal sides and 4 square corners.

p.title: Sides of each shape
p.challenge: How many straight sides does each shape have? Make the bars show it. (The corners are the same number!)
Two paper strips are joined at one end. Open them to make a SQUARE corner, like the corner of a book.
p.winText: That is a square corner! It fits the corner of a book exactly.

p.label: matchsticks
p.challenge: 1 square needs 4 matchsticks, 2 in a row need 7, 3 in a row need only 10 (they share sides). How many sticks for 6 squares in a row?
Fold a round paper plate in half, then in half again. Where the folds cross is the centre. Tap the centre of the circle!

p.title: Sides of each shape
p.challenge: Odd one out: square, rectangle, triangle. Compare the number of sides and tap the odd one out.
A (top-left) and B (bottom-right) are opposite corners of a rectangle. Go across from one and down from the other. Tap the 2 missing corners!
A stall has 260 balloons. Count on in tens to 300. How many more balloons are needed?
Build six hundred eight. Which place needs a 0?
365 = 300 + 65 = 360 + 5 = 300 + 60 + 5. Build 365 and read its expanded form.
Number slider: start at 318. Add 2, then take away 10. Watch which digit changes!
The next hundred after 347 is 400. Hop 3 ones to 350, then 50 to 400. How far is it in all?
Place 216: find 210, then go 6 steps past it.
A tray holds 100 laddoos in 10 rows of 10. It has 7 full rows. Fill the tray! How many more laddoos did you add?
The ground row has houses 301 to 310. Going up one floor adds 10. Hop from house 304 up 2 floors.
Pack 342 sweets: boxes of 100 first, then boxes of 10, then loose sweets.
Build 600 + 40 + 2. Which digit is in the hundreds place?
Compare 512 and 498. Drag the frog from 498 to 512. 5 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds!

p.title: Numbers from 4, 5 and 6
p.challenge: These are all the 3-digit numbers made with 4, 5 and 6 (each once). Put them from smallest to biggest.
Each rakhi needs 2 flowers. Seema has 14 flowers. Add a row of 2 for each rakhi until all 14 are used. How many rakhis?
Meena makes 4 rakhis with 5 beads each. Hop 4 jumps of 5. 4 × 5 = ?
Share 20 kaju katlis on 5 plates. Put one on each plate in turn until all are used. How many on each plate?
Diwali diyas: make 4 rows with 6 diyas in each row. How many diyas? Then press Turn: is 6 × 4 the same?
Each hand has 5 fingers. Add hands one row at a time, skip counting by 5s. How many fingers on 6 hands?
Jump by 6s: 6, 12, 18 ... Which jump lands on 24? That tells you 4 × 6 = 24.
To reach 24 with equal jumps, you can jump by 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 or 12. Find every array of 24 stars to see why!

p.label: numbers
p.challenge: The 5 table: 5, 10, 15, 20 ... Even number × 5 ends in 0. Does 8 × 5 end in 0 or 5? Find the 8th number.
Saving ₹5 a day for 8 days. Put in one ₹5 coin for each day. How much is saved?
Bhim counts 24 cow legs. Each cow has 4 legs. Hop by 4s to 24. How many cows?
Tiku the frog starts at 42 and jumps back by 7. How many jumps to reach 0?
4 coconuts at ₹30 each cost 4 × 30 = ₹120. The buyer pays ₹200. Give the change!
Share 23 shells equally among 5 friends. How many does each get? How many are left over?
Kabir shares 15 marbles equally among 5 friends. Give one to each, again and again. How many each?
Joseph cuts a roti into 2 equal pieces and eats one. Shade the part he ate. What part is it?
Fold the paper! Tap each dashed line to fold. Which folds give two matching halves? (Does the corner-to-corner fold work for a rectangle?)
Is three quarters of a glass more than half or less than half? Shade 3/4 and 1/2, then pick the sign.
Amit and Bala share 7 mangoes. Give one to each again and again. What is left over? (Cut it in half to keep it fair!)
Guess who I am: double me is 14. Start at 7 and hop 7 more. Do you land on 14? The jump from a number to its double is the number itself!
A watermelon is cut into 4 equal slices. Riya eats 1 slice and Arjun eats 2. Shade what they ate together.
2 quarters make a half! Cut the bottom bar into 4 equal parts and shade as much as 1/2.
12 balloons. Put them in 4 equal groups and pick one group. Is 3 balloons a half or a quarter of 12?
3 quarters + 1 quarter = ? Build the answer bar. Do you get one whole?
Count in hundreds from 500: 600, 700 ... Hop until you reach 1000. 10 hundreds make 1000!
Show 620 with hundred tiles, ten strips and small squares. How many small squares do you need?
How much must be added to 667 to reach 700? Hop +3 to 670, then +10 three times.
Tambola clue: I am between 800 and 900. My tens digit is 0. My ones digit is 5. Drag the frog to me!

p.label: numbers
p.challenge: 900, 875, 850 ... goes down by 25 each time. What is the 6th number?
Each bead is a slip of 100, 10 or 1. Make 321. Count your slips: is it 6? (3 + 2 + 1 = 6)

p.title: Smallest to greatest
p.challenge: Order 525, 552, 255 and 522 from smallest to greatest. Compare hundreds, then tens, then ones.
Secret code: red card = 100, blue = 10, yellow = 1. 4 red, 0 blue, 7 yellow. Build the number!
A school has 213 boys and 245 girls. Start at 213. Jump 2 hundreds, 4 tens and 5 ones. How many children?
Meena has 178 shells and Joseph has 145. Add 145 to 178. Carry when the ones or tens make 10!
A shop had 430 kites and sold 185. Take away 185. No ones? Break a ten. Not enough tens? Break a hundred.

p.title: Spans to measure the table

ask.question: Who has the bigger hand span?

p.challenge: The same table: Teacher measures 6 spans, Riya measures 9 spans. Who has the bigger hand span? (Bigger hand, fewer spans!)
One box side = 1 string. Make a board 4 strings wide and 2 strings tall. How many strings go around the border? (top + bottom + 2 sides)
Complete the moustache! Make the other half the same length, on the other side of the middle line.

p.title: Compared with 1 metre
p.challenge: Sort: a bed, a door, an eraser, a pencil, a shoe, a metre rod. How many are longer than, shorter than and about 1 metre?
Leela jumps a 1 metre rope + a half-metre rope + a quarter-metre rope. Drag the frog to where she lands (in metres).

p.label: numbers
p.challenge: 3, 7, 11, 15 ... Find the rule. What is the 10th number?
A door is a long rectangle. Tap the dashed lines to fold it. How many lines of symmetry does it have?

p.title: Glasses filled
p.challenge: A jug fills 6 glasses. A bottle fills 4 of the same glasses. Which holds more? Tap it.
A bucket holds 10 mugs of water. A pot holds 4 mugs. Count on from 4 to 10. How many more mugs does the bucket hold?
1 glass takes 3 ladles of buttermilk. Add a row of 3 for each glass. How many ladles fill 4 glasses?
Pour 2 quarter-litre cups into a jug. Build the answer bar: how much of a litre is that?
Bag A has 5 books and Bag B has 3. Share all 8 books so both bags weigh the same. How many books moved from A to B?
A shopkeeper puts two half-kilogram weights on one pan. Add 1/2 + 1/2. What weight is that?
A milkman has 20 litres of milk. He sells 12 litres. Hop back to find how many litres are left.

p.title: Find the heavy ball
p.challenge: Three balls look the same but one is heavier. Use the balance only ONCE to find it!

nodes.text: Put ball 1 and ball 2 on the pans

nodes.info: If the pans balance, ball 1 and ball 2 weigh the same.

nodes.text: Ball on the lower pan is heavy

p.challenge: Kishan's nursery: add 364 + 52. The tens make 11 tens: 10 of them become a hundred!
Subtract 230 − 75 with blocks. Break a ten for the ones, then break a hundred for the tens.
Start at 467. Add 10, then add 1, then add 100. Where do you land?
A pen costs ₹25 and a pencil box costs ₹60. Jump from 25 to 60. How much more is the pencil box?
Aisha has one ₹50 note, two ₹10 notes and one ₹5 coin. Put them on the counter. How much money?
Make ₹500 with ₹100 and ₹200 notes only (no coins). Can you find two different ways?
Harpreet buys a kite for ₹25 and a spool of thread for ₹40. Put them in the basket and pay the total.
Arjun gives ₹100 for a book that costs ₹65. Give his change. Count up from ₹65 to check!
Ravi saved ₹45 + ₹60 + ₹75 = ₹180. Show ₹180 with ₹100 notes and ₹10 notes.
389 is closest to which hundred? Its tens digit is 8, so round up. Drag the frog to that hundred.
Mentally: 600 − 82. Hop back 80 in tens, then 2 in ones.
School closes after 10 June. The holidays are 12 days: the 11th to the 22nd. Tap the date school reopens!
12 November 2026 is a Thursday. The same day comes again every 7 days. Tap the next Thursday.
Mira was born in 2018. Hop one year at a time to 2026. How old is she after her birthday in 2026?
Count days: from 3 June to 20 June. Tap 20 June and read how many days it is.
Show half past 4: the long hand on 6, the short hand between 4 and 5.
Show quarter to 8. Where must the long hand point? Where is the short hand?

p.title: My day
p.challenge: Put the day in order with sensible times.
panels: Wake up at about 6:30 in the morning
Go to school at 8 in the morning
Eat lunch at 1 in the afternoon
Eat dinner at 8 in the evening
Go to sleep at 9 at night

p.challenge: Move the long hand from 12 to 4. Each number is 5 minutes. How many minutes have passed?
A digital clock shows 6:45. Make the hands of the clock show the same time. Say it in words!
Is a kite symmetrical? Tap the dashed lines to fold it. Find the line where both sides match.
Mala B R B | B R B: the blue beads are coloured. Colour the right half so the mala reads the same from both ends.
Complete the rangoli! Copy each dot on the other side of the fold line, at the same distance.
Finish the mask with a mirror image. The other eye must be the same distance from the middle line.
The left side had 7 balls and the right side 3. Share all 10 so both sides match. How many balls had to move across?

p.title: Favourite ride

ask.question: How many friends did Riya ask in all?

p.challenge: Giant wheel 9, Merry-go-round 6, Toy train 5. Which ride is liked the most? And how many friends did Riya ask in all?

p.title: Kites sold (🪁 = 5 kites)

ask.question: How many kites did Arjun sell?

p.challenge: Read the key first: 🪁 = 5 kites. Arjun has 3 kites in his row. How many kites did he sell?
20 clay pots are packed with 5 pots in each box. Add one box (row of 5) at a time. How many boxes are needed?
Put them on the balance. The heavier side goes down. Which is the heaviest? (Big is not always heavy!)
Fill the bucket using a 1-litre bottle. Count the bottles. How many litres does it hold?
Lay the 1-metre rope along the mat again and again, end to end. How many metres long is the mat?

p.title: Same value
p.challenge: Think, do not calculate! Join each pair that has the same value.

p.title: Days, weeks and years
p.challenge: Join each one to the right number of days.

p.title: The 7 tangram pieces
p.challenge: A tangram is a square cut into 7 pieces. Join each piece to how many there are.
